title: What If a Spacecraft Ran on Sunlight Alone? One Did

scenes.text: What if a spacecraft needed no fuel at all? The push is weaker than a paperclip's weight.
Sunlight carries momentum. A big, thin mirror catches it, the way a sail catches wind.
LightSail 2 had a sail of 32 square meters, about the size of a boxing ring.
The craft itself was only the size of a loaf of bread, riding up in June 2019.
The push was tiny, but it never stopped, and the orbit climbed by up to a few hundred meters a day.
Sunlight alone moved a spacecraft for years. Fuel runs out. Sunshine won't, for billions of years.
